title: Dynamic Uplift Index and True‑Up Smoothing Framework for Multi‑Year Contracts
creator: Priya Nair
description: Problem: Enterprise customers on committed multi-year plans frequently request either large one-time true-ups at renewal or ad-hoc uplift negotiations mid-term. This creates unpredictable revenue recognition, long legal cycles, and churn risk when customers feel pricing is not proportional to usage growth. Goal: design a predictable, audit-friendly uplift and true-up mechanism that reduces negotiation friction, smooths customer billing volatility, and aligns renewals with security questionnaire expectations for contract terms. This ticket defines a pricing framework (Dynamic Uplift Index + True-Up Smoothing Corridor), runbook for sales and legal, and acceptance metrics for a pilot with North American mid-market customers.
background: Current state: multiple one-off uplift negotiations, manual true-ups at renewal, varied discounts across deals, and time-consuming security questionnaire alignment for multi-year commitments. Sales feedback: customers want visibility into how uplift will be calculated and prefer smoothing to avoid large end-of-term bills. Finance feedback: prefer predictable revenue recognition with smaller periodic true-ups versus lump-sum reconciliations. Product/legal feedback: need guardrails so uplift calculations are auditable and compatible with SOWs and security questionnaires.
proposed_solution: Introduce two complementary mechanisms: (1) Dynamic Uplift Index (DUI): an algorithmic multiplier applied to committed units each billing period based on observed trailing-3-month usage growth and pre-agreed growth bands. The DUI is capped and floored per contract to protect both parties. (2) True-Up Smoothing Corridor (TSC): instead of a single end-of-term reconciliation, allow quarterly or semi-annual micro-true-ups that keep per-period overage below a configurable corridor (e.g., +/-10%-25%). For multi-year deals, offer incremental graduated discounts when customers pre-commit to rolling year-on-year floors to reduce effective uplift. All terms are documented in an appendix that maps to security questionnaire SLC/contract clauses for auditability.
pricing_mechanics: High-level formula: uplift_factor = clamp(1 + alpha * trailing_growth_pct, floor, cap). alpha is a tunable sensitivity parameter (default 0.6). Example: trailing_growth_pct=20% -> uplift_factor = clamp(1 + 0.6*0.20, 1.00, 1.15) = 1.12. Quarterly true-up = max(0, billed_commit * (observed_usage/commit - 1)) * uplift_factor. Smoothing corridor rule: if quarterly true-up > corridor_threshold, auto-spread remainder over next two quarters subject to cap. Discounts for 2-year and 3-year commitments: apply graduated decrement to uplift_factor cap (e.g., cap - 2% for 2yr, cap - 4% for 3yr). All numeric parameters are configurable per account.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (pilot definition): finalize parameters and legal appendix (2 weeks). Phase 1 (pilot pilot): enable for 12 mid-market customers in NA on new contracts (Q2 2026). Phase 2 (sales + finance rollout): train AE and finance on runbook, update quote templates and billing engine (Q3 2026). Phase 3 (scale): expand to ERPs and larger accounts after validation (Q4 2026). Pilot success gate: implementable in billing system, legal signoff, and NRR impact within forecast tolerance.
metrics: Key metrics to track during pilot: (1) Number of uplift negotiations initiated per ARR bucket, (2) Average size of true-up per account and distribution, (3) Renewal conversion rate for pilot cohort vs control, (4) Net Revenue Retention (NRR) delta, (5) Time-to-contract signature for renewals, (6) CSAT/renewal NPS changes, (7) Number of security questionnaire exceptions triggered.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Customers perceive algorithm as opaque -> Mitigation: publish worked examples and a contractual disclosure appendix. Risk: Billing engine complexity -> Mitigation: confine pilot to accounts where billing is managed by finance with technical support; implement feature flags. Risk: Legal pushback on auto-spreading charges -> Mitigation: optionality — customers can opt-out of smoothing corridor for fixed true-up. Risk: Accounting recognition complexity -> Mitigation: involve finance early and create revenue recognition mapping playbook.
stakeholder_notes: Stakeholders: Sales (Aaron Park), Finance (Sofia Martinez), Legal (Emily Zhao), Security & Compliance (Markus Berg). Sales asked for a simple one-pager to share with buyers; finance requires GL mapping and sample amortization. Security team requires explicit contract language tying uplift rules to billing cadence to answer security questionnaire items about billing frequency and audit trail.
acceptance_criteria: Legal appendix approved by Legal and Security (signed redlines)
Billing implementation feature flag created and verified in staging with sample accounts
Pilot cohort of >=10 customers onboarded with signed amendments or new SOWs
Dashboard tracking uplift, true-ups, and corridor breaches in Redwood Console
NRR impact for pilot cohort within +/-3% of forecast (first 6 months)
open_questions: What default alpha and corridor thresholds should we use for pilot? (proposed: alpha=0.6, corridor=15%)
Should smoothing be opt-in or opt-out by default for existing customers?
How should we reflect smoothing and micro-true-ups in security questionnaires (SOW appendix vs separate billing annex)?
Are there GAAP/IFRS revenue recognition constraints we must embed as mandatory terms?

decision_record: Provisional decision: proceed with pilot using alpha=0.6, corridor=15%, quarterly micro-true-ups, graduated discount caps for 2/3 year commitments. Final parameterization pending legal/accounting review.
